tips.title: Scribing Panel Lines with RB Productions Tools
tips.text: For crisp panel lines, use RB Productions scribing tools. Hold the tool perpendicular to the surface, apply gentle pressure, and pull straight towards you. Start from one edge and scribe along the length of the panel. For deep scribing, use the larger tool first, then follow up with the smaller tool. Always scribe away from delicate details to avoid accidentally damaging them.

tips.title: Photo-Etch Bending with Eduard Bending Jigs
tips.text: Eduard photo-etch bending jigs allow precise bending without breaking. Place the jig on a flat surface, then position the photo-etch part over the desired angle. Using tweezers, carefully bend the part along the jig's edge. Apply even pressure and bend incrementally to avoid breaking the part. For 90° bends, use the corner of the jig.

tips.title: Airbrush Needle Cleaning with Iwata Brush Cleaner
tips.text: Keep your Iwata airbrush performing smoothly with regular needle cleaning. After each use, remove the needle, soak it in Iwata Brush Cleaner for 15 minutes, then scrub it gently with a soft toothbrush. Rinse with warm water and dry thoroughly before reassembling. Once a month, soak the needle overnight in cleaner to remove tougher residues.

tips.title: Masking with Tamiya Masking Tape vs Kabuki Tape
tips.text: Tamiya Masking Tape is great for sharp edges, but can leave residue. Kabuki Tape is easier to remove but may fray. For best results, use Tamiya for sharp edges and Kabuki for curved surfaces. Always cut Kabuki tape with scissors for cleaner edges. Before applying, lightly score the tape's backing with a knife to make it easier to tear.

tips.title: Sanding Stick Progression for Smooth Surfaces
tips.text: Achieve smooth surfaces using a progression of sanding sticks from Arma Hobby. Start with 240 grit, followed by 400, then 600 grit. Wet-sand in one direction, using light pressure and a firm, steady hand. After each grit, wipe off residue with a damp cloth and check for any missed areas. For hard-to-reach places, use folded sanding paper held with tweezers.
